remediation.fix_approach: Added stopHostScreenUpdate() calls at the two active logout paths: (1) NavigationService.errorHandler() before storageService.setNotConnected(), (2) AppComponent.logout() disconnectSubscription teardown callback.
remediation.root_cause: stopHostScreenUpdate() was defined and implemented correctly (clears setInterval and nulls intervalId) but had zero call sites in the entire codebase. The VULN-020 fix added the method but never wired it up. The 5-second polling interval continued indefinitely after logout. The isConnected() guard prevented actual API calls, but the interval remained active and wasted event-loop cycles.
changes_made: src/app/services/navigation/navigation.service.ts errorHandler(): call this.stopHostScreenUpdate() before this.storageService.setNotConnected() in the redirect-to-webLogin branch
src/app/app.component.ts logout(): changed disconnectSubscription.add callback to call this.navigationService.stopHostScreenUpdate() then this.storageService.setNotConnected()
remediation.verification_needed: After logout, verify no setInterval callbacks fire. Can be checked in DevTools Performance panel or by adding a temporary debug log to checkScreenUpdated() and verifying it stops after logout.
remediation.defense_in_depth: isConnected() guard in checkScreenUpdated() prevents API calls even if interval somehow survives — belt-and-suspenders approach.
remediation.testing: 1. Login, wait for polling to start. 2. Logout. 3. Verify polling stops (no new checkScreenUpdated calls). 4. Re-login — verify polling restarts correctly.
remediation.residual_risk: Low. AbstractUserExits error paths (HTTP 410 Gone) also call setNotConnected() without stopHostScreenUpdate() — these are error/disconnect scenarios where the isConnected() guard will already be false, making the interval functionally inert.
